linkedin.activityText: Activity 3M followers Posts No more previous content Ankur Warikoo Ankur Warikoo 22m Ankur Warikoo shared this 20 signs that you are doing better than you think you are: 1. You paid the bills this month and maybe something more for non-essentials as well. 2. You questioned yourself. You feel miserable some days. This means you are still open to growth. 3. You have an income. You are earning money that helps you sleep, eat, and wear something. 4. You have time to do something that you enjoy. Even if it is lying on the couch, watching Netflix. 5. You are not worried about where your next meal is coming from. 6. You can eat for pleasure. It is not a matter of sheer survival for you. 7. You have 1 or 2 truly close friends. And you realise that may be enough. 8. You can afford the smallest conveniences - a metro ride, Uber/Ola, or a cup of coffee at your favourite cafe. 9. You are not the same person you were a year ago. 10. You have the time and means to do something beyond the bare minimum. You have recently read a book, gone to a concert, worked out, or taken a day trip. 11. You have a selection of clothing you can choose from. Or it was a choice not to. You are in a position to decide. 12. You can sense what is not right in your life. You may not know how to solve for it yet, but you know something is off. 13. If you talk to your younger self, you would be able to say "we did it." 14. You have a space of your own. Doesn't need to be a home or apartment. Could be a sofa, or a corner, or a desk. 15. You have chosen to break away from toxic relationships. 16. You are interested in something. Something that excites you and intrigues you. 17. You know how to take care of yourself. How many hours of sleep you should get, what to do for fun, who you can turn to during tough times. 18. You are working towards a goal. Something that drives you; that motivates you even if it doesn't come with any potential reward. 19. You are not set on only one future version of yourself. You allow yourself to be flexible. 20. You have been through crap and have survived. Life didn't get easier. You got stronger. Ankur Warikoo Ankur Warikoo 5h Ankur Warikoo shared this Does success remove your insecurity? I used to believe it would. It doesn't. It just relocates it. Before success, the fear is: "Will this even work?" After success, the fear becomes: "Can I do it again?" And after repeated success, it turns into: "What if I lose all of it?" The mind simply upgrades its fears with every achievement. It never runs out of new ones to hand you. Which is why chasing success for emotional peace is a rigged game. You think the calm is waiting on the other side of the next milestone. It isn't. You get there and the finish line quietly moves again. The peace was never something success could give you. It has to be built now. Alongside the chase. Not after it. posts.caption:
Suppose you have ₹100 and ₹10 of it goes missing.

Would you spend the remaining ₹90 trying to find that ₹10?

No, right?

So when someone at the age of 24, 25, or 27 asks this question - “I’m not enjoying my career. But it’s too late. I won’t be able to change your career now.” 

Then is it the right question or not?

I remember I started my career as a scientist at the age of 24.

At 25, I was building corporate training programs.
At 26, I was a consultant.
At 29, I became an entrepreneur.
At 31, I joined an MNC.
At 35, I started my own startup.
At 40, I started content creation.

Today, again, I am running my own startup.

In a 20-year career, I have changed my career multiple times.

Because I know that 10 years have passed - that’s not important. 
The 30 years ahead matter more.

We think interesting people are living some thrilling, unpredictable lives.

The truth is the opposite.

The person you find fascinating reads every day. 
Trains every day. 
Follows the same routine everyday. 
Shows up for the same unglamorous work long after the excitement wears off.

The boring, repetitive things nobody claps for.

That’s exactly what makes them interesting. 
The depth, the skill, the range you admire was built in all those dull, repeated hours.

Everyone wants the interesting life.
Almost no one wants the boring days that build it.

3 settings on your phone that can save you money.

1/ Your bank apps have transaction controls.

You can set how much the limit is for domestic online transactions, domestic ATM transactions, international transactions, and international ATM transactions.

2/ Never let your OTPs appear on your lock screen.

In both Android and iOS, you can change your notification settings.

3/ Go to the AutoPay or Mandate section of your UPI app.

There you will find countless recurring mandates that you may have forgotten, but they keep getting deducted every month.

3 simple things that can save your money.

Clear any interview with this 5-day challenge.

On Day 1 - prepare your 90-second introduction.

You have to focus on 4 things:
What are you doing right now?
What relevant experience do you have?
What are the things you are really good at?
And what do you want to do next?

Day 2 - design your proof.

This is all the evidence you can show a recruiter if they need any proof - proof of your work, internships, experience, and knowledge too.

Day 3 - practice stress interviews.

Pick your most powerful, strongest story or strength. Put it into ChatGPT and tell it to ask you follow-up stress questions. Answer them without preparing.

Day 4 - learn to answer a question whose answer you don’t know.

Upload your resume to ChatGPT and ask it to pose 30 questions that are not obvious, very difficult, and almost out of syllabus, and try to answer all of them.

Day 5 - do a 20-minute mock interview.

Activate ChatGPT voice and tell it your full context, and then say, “Take an interview in English.”

This 5-day training and preparation can help you prepare for every interview.

We grow up believing our parents are meant to have all the answers.

So when they get something wrong, we hold it against them for years.

But they were figuring out life for the first time too. 
With their own fears, their own wounds, their own parents they were still healing from.

They were never perfect beings.

They were just people, doing their best with what they knew at the time.

The day you start seeing your parents as humans first, a lot of your anger quietly turns into understanding.

If a friend or relative asks you for money, how do you handle it without making things awkward?

These 5 rules can help.

1/ Never lend more than you are comfortable losing.

2/ If you can give the money, don’t treat it as a loan. 
Tell yourself, “If I get it back, that’s great, but I assume this money won’t come back.”

3/ If you cannot lend the money, say so directly. 
If you beat around the bush, it will make things awkward.

4/ For large amounts, always put it in writing.

5/ Never lend money again to someone who hasn’t returned it the first time.

A girl went to college and forgot her parents. 
After many days, she wrote them a letter:

“Maa, Papa, before you read this, I want you to sit down. I wanted to tell you that as soon as I went to college, my room caught fire. 

I had to jump out of my window to save my life. 

God bless the boy who came running and saved my life. 
He would come to see me in the hospital. 
We became friends and I don’t know when that friendship turned into love. 

Now, we are married. 
There was no hurry, but my pregnancy is visible now. 
And I didn’t want it to show at the wedding.

Maa, Papa, please listen carefully. 

There was no fire, I don’t have a boyfriend, I am not pregnant, and whatever I said was not true. 

I just failed all my exams.”

Now, see how quickly this letter changed. 
But why? 

Because perspective is everything. 

If the daughter straight away told them that she failed, then that wouldn’t have worked. 

But suddenly, seeing all these things, the parents would have said, “You just failed. 
No problem, work harder next time.” 

Perspective changes everything!
Share this with someone who would find this helpful.
Everybody is jealous of the destination. Nobody is jealous of the journey.
